input: Brainstorm a name for my new bakery

candidate.taskDescription: Generate a unique and appealing name for your new bakery.

questions.title: What type of bakery would you like to specialize in?
questions.description: e.g., artisanal bread, vegan pastries, or cupcakes.

questions.title: Do you have a preferred theme or style for the bakery's branding?
questions.description: e.g., rustic, modern, vintage.

questions.title: What type of baked goods would you like to focus on?
What message or values would you like the bakery's name to convey?
questions.description: e.g., freshness, quality, community.

questions.title: Are there any specific words or phrases you would like to include in the name?
questions.description: e.g., 'Sweet Treats', 'Bakery Bliss', 'Local Flavors'.

questions.title: How long would you like the bakery's name to be?
questions.description: e.g., 3-5 words.

questions.title: Have you considered any existing bakery names in the area or similar industries?
questions.description: e.g., 'Flour & Frost', 'Bakes & Brews', 'Sweet Haven'.

verdict.notes: Set B's biggest weakness is redundancy: Q1 ("type of bakery") and Q3 ("type of baked goods") ask nearly the same thing, wasting a question slot. This gap in non-redundancy also hurts coverage, as important unknowns like target customer, personal/story-based naming, and location (competitive landscape) go unasked. Q6 (name length) is a very minor, low-value detail that feels generic rather than insightful.

candidate.taskDescription: Gather essential information to find the right used car.

questions.title: What is your budget for the car?
questions.description: Include both the purchase price and any additional costs like taxes or registration.

questions.title: Do you have a preferred make or model?
questions.description: Consider factors like fuel efficiency, reliability, and resale value.

questions.title: What is your driving preference?
questions.description: Urban commuting, long-distance travel, or off-road?

questions.title: How many passengers do you typically have?
questions.description: This affects the size and type of vehicle you'll need.

questions.title: Do you need additional features like air conditioning or navigation?
questions.description: These can impact both comfort and cost.

questions.title: Have you owned a car before?
questions.description: This can provide insights into your driving habits and preferences.

questions.title: What is your preferred method of transportation?
questions.description: Car, public transit, biking, or walking?

verdict.notes: Set B misses critical car-buying unknowns (mileage tolerance, vehicle age, location, financing) and replaces them with vague or tangential questions like "driving preference," "prior car ownership," and "preferred method of transportation" that don't directly inform a used-car purchase plan. Its coverage of genuinely important unknowns is weak compared to Set A.

questions.title: Do you have any specific preferences for therapists?
questions.description: e.g., gender, experience level, specialties.

questions.description: e.g., qualifications, reviews, communication style.

verdict.notes: Set B is too vague and generic — questions like "Do you have any specific preferences?" and "Have you considered any specific criteria for evaluating a therapist?" are near-meaningless filler that don't surface actionable information. It also misses critical unknowns like who the therapy is for, the modality preference (in-person vs. online), and urgency, while overlapping on preference/criteria questions.

Coverage of what actually matters (current resume, target job posting, seniority level, timeline) is poor.

input: Untangle my German tax returns for 2020-2024

candidate.taskDescription: A structured approach to organizing and analyzing German tax returns for 2020-2024.

questions.title: Which tax software or tools do you currently use to manage your German taxes?
Have you already created or reviewed a consolidated 2020-2024 tax return for each year?
questions.description: Optional: Do you have a draft or completed return for 2020-2024?

questions.title: What is your preferred method for organizing your tax documents (digital or physical)?
questions.description: Optional: Do you have a system in place for storing and accessing your documents?

questions.title: Are there any specific financial transactions or income sources that you want to focus on during this process?
questions.description: Optional: Do you have any outstanding tax liabilities or refunds to address?

questions.title: Have you identified any discrepancies or areas of concern in your tax returns for the past years?
questions.description: Optional: Have you consulted with a tax professional for any advice or clarification?

questions.title: What is your timeline for completing this tax return organization and analysis?
questions.description: Optional: Are there any deadlines or milestones you need to meet?

questions.title: Do you require any additional resources or support during this process, such as a tax professional or specialized software?
questions.description: Optional: Are there any specific challenges or complexities you are facing?

verdict.notes: Set B asks mostly generic project-management questions (preferred organization method, timeline, additional resources) that could apply to almost any administrative task, and misses critical German-tax-specific unknowns like residency status, employment type, Finanzamt registration, and whether documents even exist. Its questions also assume a level of prior engagement ("Have you already created a consolidated return?") that is unlikely given the user said they need to "untangle" things, making them feel out of touch with the user's actual situation.

verdict.notes: Set B wastes two of its seven questions on narrow vendor-specific details (photographer/videographer and catering) while missing the single most critical unknown — budget — which is foundational to every other wedding planning decision.
